Figure raises questions about deal with France despite UK ministers insisting repeat arrivals will be removed

Almost 50 asylum seekers deported using the “one in one out” scheme have been recorded as returning to the UK a second time, the Guardian has learned.

In addition to the returnees detained by the Home Office, an unknown number are believed to have arrived in the UK undetected.

Continue reading...

events.title: Danish pupils will have to orally defend essays in attempt to combat AI cheating
events.summary:
Government introduces several measures, including monitoring of computers, for pupils aged 16 to 19

  • Europe live – latest updates

Danish teenagers will have to make an oral defence of their written essays to combat AI cheating, the government has announced.

Pupils aged 16 to 19 at upper secondary school (known in Denmark as gymnasiet) will also be encouraged to do written assignments at school under controlled conditions, including monitoring of their computer screens, rather than at home.

events.title: Israel charges West Bank settler over death of renowned Palestinian activist
events.summary:
Yinon Levi faces trial for reckless manslaughter related to the 2025 killing of Awdah Hathaleen

Israeli prosecutors have charged a Jewish settler over the killing of a Palestinian community leader in the occupied West Bank last year – the ⁠first such indictment in nearly three years.

In papers filed by the state attorney’s office, Yinon Levi is charged with reckless manslaughter in the death of Awdah Hathaleen, a prominent ⁠activist who was involved in the 2025 Oscar-winning documentary No Other Land.

Continue reading...

events.title: Trump’s Gaza Board of Peace issues first building contract – for a military base
events.summary:
Exclusive: Louisiana firm awarded tender to build rudimentary outpost to house Moroccan troops

Donald Trump’s Board of Peace, which was set up in January to oversee the reconstruction of Gaza, has finally issued its first construction contract in the devastated territory: a project to build a rudimentary 150-person military outpost to house Moroccan troops, a source familiar with the matter told the Guardian.

The contract, which has not yet been finalised, was awarded to Arkel International, a Louisiana-based firm that has previously carried out work with the US government in countries such as Iraq.

Continue reading...

events.title: Top Democrats accuse Trump officials over Israeli settlers’ ‘unbridled violence’
events.summary:
Letter says lifting of sanctions sent ‘clear message’ settlers can use deadly force in West Bank without consequences

Senior Democrats have accused Donald Trump’s administration of giving a green light to violent Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank, warning that its policies created “a climate of impunity and unbridled violence” that endangers both Palestinians and US citizens.

In a letter seen by the Guardian, a group of 19 Democratic senators and representatives call for the restoration of sanctions against extremist settlers and demand independent US investigations into the deaths of nine US citizens killed in the West Bank since 2022.

Continue reading...

events.title: Israeli strike that killed journalist in Lebanon was war crime, say rights groups
events.summary:
Investigation by Human Rights Watch, Amnesty and Legal Agenda shows Israel deliberately attacked Amal Khalil and colleague Zeinab Faraj knowing they were civilians

An Israeli strike that killed Lebanese journalist Amal Khalil and injured her colleague Zeinab Faraj in April was a war crime, three rights organisations said on Thursday.

Investigations from Human Rights Watch (HRW), Amnesty International and Legal Agenda showed that Israel deliberately and directly attacked Khalil and Faraj, with apparent knowledge that they were civilians. The organisations called for the attacks to be investigated as war crimes, while HRW called for states to halt arm sales to Israel and put targeted sanctions on Israeli officials responsible for ongoing crimes.

Continue reading...

events.title: India-Bangladesh relations hit new low over exiled PM’s speech to press in Delhi
events.summary:
Dhaka accuses India of giving platform to a ‘convicted genocider’ by allowing Sheikh Hasina to address journalists

Bangladesh has lashed out at India for allowing the ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina to address journalists in New Delhi, plunging already strained bilateral relations to a fresh low.

Dhaka accused India of giving a platform to a fugitive it labelled a “convicted genocider” and of undermining efforts to repair ties, after Hasina vowed to return to Bangladesh in December despite facing a death sentence on charges of “crimes against humanity”.

Continue reading...

events.title: High-profile Indian journalist jailed for 10 years for raping colleague
events.summary:
Tarun Tejpal, ex-editor of Tehelka magazine, was initially acquitted in 2021 in case that drew nationwide attention

An Indian court has sentenced a high-profile former editor of an investigative news magazine to 10 years in prison after convicting him of raping a junior colleague, overturning his acquittal in a case that drew nationwide attention.

Tarun Tejpal, 63, the founder and former editor of Tehelka magazine, was accused of raping a journalist in the lift of a five-star hotel in the western coastal state of Goa during an event in November 2013. He was arrested and spent seven months in jail until the supreme court granted him bail.

Continue reading...

events.title: Exiled PM vows to return to Bangladesh despite execution threat
events.summary:
Sheikh Hasina plans a December comeback two years after being ousted in a bloody uprising led by students

Bangladesh’s ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina has vowed to return home by the end of the year, even though she faces a death sentence.

“They may put me in a cell. They may kill me. Anything may happen, but still I have to go,” said Hasina, two years after a student-led uprising toppled her government.

Continue reading...

events.title: Pakistani authorities ban international media from reporting in most of country
events.summary:
Rules brought in soon after killing of dozens of protesters, news of which was reported only by overseas outlets

Pakistani authorities have imposed severe new restrictions on international media, including barring them from reporting in most of the country, in a move that has provoked a significant backlash from journalist organisations.

According to the new rules anyone, including Pakistani nationals, should seek permission first if they want to report from anywhere in Pakistan except three cities – Islamabad, Karachi and Lahore.

Continue reading...

events.title: Pakistan precinct suspends all 78 officers and staff over alleged rape at police station
events.summary:
Lahore police official says all personnel were responsible for preventing and reporting any wrongdoing at station

The alleged rape of a 20-year-old woman with learning disabilities in a police station in Lahore, Pakistan, has prompted authorities to suspend all 78 police officers and staff at the precinct, in one of the country’s biggest ever disciplinary actions against its police force.

The woman alleges that an assistant sub-inspector apprehended her, took her to Ghaziabad police station and raped her in a room on the second floor. The woman’s family said she disappeared on the street, before returning home in tears and stating that she had been sexually assaulted at the station.

Continue reading...

events.title: Primary schools to be told to identify children at risk of future unemployment
events.summary:
Exclusive: Neet crisis review to call for teachers to be asked to spot those at risk of leaving education jobless at 16

  • What can Dublin teach us? Milburn goes on quest to learn

Primary schools in England should be required to identify children at risk of leaving education at 16 without finding a job, a government review is to recommend.

Alan Milburn, who is leading a review into Britain’s crisis in youth worklessness, said he would call for sweeping changes in education policy alongside a shake-up of the benefits system to address the problem.

Continue reading...

events.title: Meet the offenders cleaning canals in the West Midlands as an alternative to prison
events.summary:
With the debate over prison overcrowding and what to do about it raging, one initiative offers an alternative solution

As the prison overcrowding crisis shows no sign of abating and the debate rages over early releases, an initiative in the West Midlands offers an alternative to custodial sentences.

The Guardian was offered rare access to the project, under which, instead of being sent to prison, convicted offenders work on the improvement of waterways and green spaces around Smethwick. It is a small part of the community payback scheme, which in total clocked up an estimated 5m hours across England and Wales in the last year.

Continue reading...

events.title: July’s heatwaves kept UK shoppers away from high street
events.summary:
Visits down 3.8% after 6.2% fall in June, with many choosing to buy online instead, research for retail body finds

Shoppers stayed away from UK high streets during last month’s heatwave temperatures, with many choosing to buy online instead as the mercury in some areas rose into the mid-30Cs.

Trips to high streets were down by 3.8% year on year in July after a 6.2% fall in June, according to research from the monitoring firm Sensormatic for the British Retail Consortium (BRC).

Continue reading...

events.title: ‘It is British life’: No 10 vows to stop councils trying to limit standing in pubs
events.summary:
Westminster council has recommended banning ‘vertical drinking’ or ordering at the bar in new draft licensing policy

No 10 has vowed to confiscate powers from local councils which try to restrict customers from standing up while drinking in pubs or ordering at the bar.

It comes after the Guardian revealed on Thursday that Westminster council in central London recommended not allowing “vertical drinking” or ordering at the bar in its new draft licensing policy.

Continue reading...

events.title: Dons call for Cambridge leaders to take blame for Jason Arday appointment
events.summary:
Exclusive: Academics call for inquiry, saying university must be held accountable for ‘grotesque racism unleashed’

The University of Cambridge’s leaders deserve blame for the “grotesque racism unleashed” by Jason Arday’s appointment as professor, according to academics calling for the university to hold an independent inquiry.

The Guardian understands that senior dons at Cambridge are circulating a joint letter calling for an inquiry into the processes and circumstances around Arday being given the position, with many suggesting the university wanted a “quick fix” to improve the diversity of its staff.

Continue reading...

events.title: Trump unbound: the making of an imperial presidency – podcast
events.summary:
Donald Trump’s second term is unlike his first. The politicians who challenged him are gone. The lawyers who once pushed back now choose their battles. events.title: Justin Pearson and Brent Taylor win primaries for key Tennessee House seat
events.summary:
Nominees to face off in November in redistricted seat central to Trump’s bid to retain slim Republican majority

Tennessee primary voters picked a pair of Memphis-area lawmakers to square off in a dramatically reconfigured US House seat central to Donald Trump’s plan to try to hold on to a slim Republican majority in the midterm congressional elections.

Republicans chose state senator Brent Taylor, who was endorsed by Trump, to be their nominee in the revamped 9th congressional district. Democrats picked state representative Justin Pearson, who gained national prominence three years ago when he was expelled from the Tennessee House for protesting in support of gun control measures.

Continue reading...

events.title: New Mexico court orders Meta to pay $567m over harms to children’s mental health
events.summary:
Ruling comes as part of second phase of landmark trial that found social media company enabled harm against users

A New Mexico court has ordered Meta, the parent company of Facebook, to pay $567m into a fund aimed at redressing adverse mental health impacts from the social media giant’s platforms.

The Thursday ruling comes as a part of the second phase of a landmark trial the social media giant lost in March. At the time, a jury found that the company knowingly harmed children’s mental health and concealed what it knew about child sexual exploitation on its platforms, and imposed the maximum penalty: a $375m fine.

Continue reading...

events.title: Trump’s birthright citizenship attack the latest effort in obsessive campaign
events.summary:
For more than a decade, president has been fixated on trying to undermine a key constitutional right

With a pair of executive orders on Thursday, Donald Trump has tried – once again – to undermine the guarantee of birthright citizenship, a right enshrined in the US constitution and reaffirmed by the supreme court just five weeks ago.

The orders attempt to broaden the categories of children who would be ineligible for automatic US citizenship and ban so-called “birth tourism”, which the president claimed is practiced by “hundreds of thousands” of people.

events.summary: The US president's move comes just two months after the Supreme Court ruled that his first executive order on citizenship was unconstitutional.

events.summary: The head of the Africa Centres for Disease Control pledged to deploy a vaccine for a previous Ebola strain in the current DRC outbreak, with test cases indicating a potentially live-saving level of protection.

events.summary: Droughts, heat and falling water levels in the Danube are hitting central and southeastern Europe hard. Hungary and Romania are experiencing an energy crisis — whereas countries like Bulgaria are better prepared.

events.summary: With over 3,000 migrants still in Ceuta after rushing the border last week, Ceuta leader Juan Jesus Vivas warns the situation in the Spanish exclave is "unsustainable." Hundreds of those migrants are minors.

events.title: Germany news: Officials deny reports of drone near munitions-laden plane
events.summary: Officials in Germany have rejected reports that an explosive-laden drone found at Leipzig airport was next to a plane filled with weapons destined for Ukraine. Federal prosecutors have taken over the case.

events.title: The Mata Hari affair: Courtesan, spy, legend
events.summary: Regarded the most famous female spy of all time, dancer Mata Hari had men falling at her feet but was executed for treason. Did she really betray state secrets?

events.title: Can UN chief's initiative kickstart resolution for Cyprus?
events.summary: UN chief Antonio Guterres considers a resolution to the Cyprus issue to be vital for regional stability and has initiated a new diplomatic effort. What are the prospects for its success?

events.title: Why Iran is sending mixed signals on talks
events.summary: Trump says talks with Iran are underway. Tehran says it is discussing the Strait of Hormuz with Oman, not Washington. Analysts say the gap reflects competing political pressures.

events.title: AfD threatens to cut funding for 'modern-thinking' culture
events.summary: The far-right party could win an absolute majority in Saxony-Anhalt's state election in September. Their cultural program denigrates Bauhaus, Holocaust remembrance culture and diversity in theater.

events.title: Germany: Leipzig airport drone attack sets off alarm bells
events.summary: German authorities have begun a counterterrorism ⁠investigation into a drone laden with explosives found near a Ukrainian transport plane at Leipzig Airport. It is seen as a "hybrid attack scenario."

events.title: Marine One: Helicopter carrying Trump flew close to passenger jet, FAA plans probe
events.summary: Trump's helicopter and a passenger jet briefly were too close near Reagan National Airport, prompting an inquiry into what happened to the safety rules adopted after last year's deadly collision.

events.title: How Gianni Infantino rose to rule football
events.summary: Gianni Infantino is staying on as FIFA president despite growing pressure to step down. So who is football's most powerful man, why did UEFA and others turn against him, and how did he reassert his authority?

events.title: Africa and the ICC: Why most countries are staying
events.summary: A new wave of African withdrawals has swept through the International Criminal Court. Chad turned its back on the court after three junta-led states in the Sahel exited. But most African countries still trust The Hague.

events.title: Munich car-ramming attacker sentenced to life in prison
events.summary: A Munich court has handed down the toughest possible sentence over the 2025 attack that killed a mother and her toddler and injured dozens more.

events.title: Germany: 10 years of 'Integration Act' for refugees
events.summary: The German Integration Act aimed to regulate the integration of recognized refugees following high levels of immigration, facilitating access to the labor market in return for integration efforts.

events.title: Middle East: Hormuz deal near, IDF soldiers dead in Lebanon
events.summary: Iran has said a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz is in its "final stage" if the US doesn't obstruct it. Two Israeli soldiers were killed in southern Lebanon.

events.title: Why is Russia selling its gold?
events.summary: Russia has become one of the world's biggest sellers of gold over the past 12 months. It's an attempt to raise cash in the face of budget issues, but not necessarily a sign of a looming financial crisis.

events.title: What's behind the Algeria-Morocco rivalry?
events.summary: Morocco and Algeria have been at odds for decades, chiefly over the territory of Western Sahara. But their rivalry now extends far beyond the territory.

events.title: Will Russia start a fresh mobilization drive?
events.summary: Russia is preparing a new mobilization campaign to boost troop numbers, Ukrainian officials and independent Russian media outlets report. The Kremlin denies this.

events.title: Germany: Court jails far-right youth terror cell members
events.summary: A Hamburg court has handed down stiff prison sentences to members of the far-right terrorist group "Last Wave of Defense." Politicians are warning that those drawn into extremist violence are getting younger.

events.title: A glowing future for nuclear power? Mini reactors explained
events.summary: Small modular reactors are seen as a flexible energy source. Their promise: abundant energy, cheap, clean and climate-friendly with lower water use. But do the numbers add up? We look at what's behind the SMR hype.

events.title: Sleep: Do you really need eight hours of shuteye?
events.summary: Every so often we hear of high-ranking politicians or CEOs claiming to get by on very little sleep — some as little as three hours a night. If they're not natural short sleepers, chances are they're heading for trouble.

events.title: Hungary's Lake Velence is drying up
events.summary: Hungary is feeling the heat. The country's third-largest lake is shrinking, the Danube is running low, and soaring temperatures could force the country's only nuclear power plant to shut down.

events.title: AI ecosystem's 'circular' investment: risk or advantage?
events.summary: Amid talk of an AI sector bubble, one aspect is under scrutiny. Many big AI players are invested in smaller ones, who then buy the bigger firm's products. This brings risks and advantages.

events.title: Italy: Garbage workers help woman find €1 million jackpot
events.summary: A woman who won €1 million mistakenly threw her lottery ticket in a trash bin in Bitonto, southern Italy — prompting her local sanitation company to launch an hourslong search.

events.title: South Sudan: How climate change can result in toxic water
events.summary: Years of flooding have resulted in disastrous water pollution in South Sudan's main oil region. As communities, scientists and health workers scramble for solutions, the long-term impacts of the crisis is yet to emerge.

events.title: Tennis star Sabalenka supports sport's new sex test policy
events.summary: The world number one women's tennis player supports the WTA's new sex testing rules. Others are more critical of the policy.

events.title: Germany news: Hedgehog triggers police alert
events.summary: Police responding to a supermarket burglar alarm in central Germany found it was caused by an unlikely culprit. Germany's flag carrier, Lufthansa, has turned in poor quarterly results. DW has more.

events.title: More cancer-prone? Why younger generations may be at risk
events.summary: Researchers are observing certain age-related types of cancer more frequently in younger people. A new study suggests this could be because younger generations are aging faster than their parents or grandparents.

events.title: Dry Danube River threatens nuclear power in Romania, Hungary
events.summary: Hungary's Paks nuclear power plant was operating at about 10% of capacity because of a lack of cooling river water. In Romania, the military blew up a rock outcrop in a bid to improve water flow to the Cernavoda plant.

events.title: Ceuta: EU calls borders a 'shared European responsibility'
events.summary: The European Commission has offered Morocco more support at the border to Ceuta and Melilla, and called for "united action" from the bloc on border security. Its interior ministers will discuss the issue on Tuesday.

events.title: Binging on cringe: It's as addictive as 'eating junk food'
events.summary: Flexing achievements? Cringe. Expressing genuine emotions? Cringe. You want to look away, but you can’t. Cringe. It's so addictive, people have built social media careers by monetizing other people's worst moments.

events.title: What happens next for Infantino and FIFA?
events.summary: FIFA President Gianni Infantino is under pressure after the failure of his plan to create a commercial subsidiary for the World Cup. But will he be ousted? And what is needed for that to happen?

events.title: Fact check: Russian disinformation targets German elections
events.summary: Ahead of four elections in Germany this fall, dozens of fake posts are circulating online aimed at discrediting candidates and portraying Germany as divided. Analysts warn that Russia is now targeting local candidates.

events.title: The economic toll of Spain's wildfires
events.summary: Devastating wildfires are ravaging Spain's tourism, economy and nature. Could the country have done more to prevent them?

events.title: Man arrested over death of British woman found in suitcase in Athens
events.summary: The body of Scottish national Elisabeth-Jane Ross was discovered last month in a suitcase in a derelict building in Athens.

events.title: Ceuta: Most who breached border have left, Spain says
events.summary: Nearly all of the more than 50,000 migrants who breached the border this week have returned to Morocco, according to Spanish officials. At least 72 people died in the border rush. DW has more.

events.title: Germany news: DB hampered by 'organized irresponsibility'
events.summary: DB chief Evelyn Palla wants to overcome the culture of ''organized irresponsibility" by empowering new decision-makers within the railway operator. Bavarian brass musicians have wrapped up a 72-hour concert. DW has more.

events.title: Moscow restaurant blast a 'brutal terror attack,' mayor says
events.summary: The deadly explosion outside an upscale Moscow restaurant at Kudrinskaya Square was a "brutal terror attack," Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said, promising the perpetrators would be punished. But many questions remain.

events.title: Poland: Prime Minister Tusk defies anti-Ukrainian violence
events.summary: Anti-Ukrainian sentiment in Poland is on the rise, with numerous attacks against refugees from the war in Ukraine. Prime Minister Donald Tusk has spoken out against the violence and warned of the danger from Russia.

events.title: Germany: Islamism and right-wing extremism — a story of mutual radicalization
events.summary: Following the attack on a Berlin Pride festival, the focus in Germany is turning to Islamist terrorism. An expert warns: Looking only at Islamists overlooks the parallels with right-wing extremism.

events.title: Germany: As temperatures rise, so does climate skepticism
events.summary: Some 98% of active climate scientists say climate change is happening, and is man-made. Nonetheless, a new study shows the number of climate-change skeptics in Germany has increased. Why is that?

events.title: On the front line of Europe's battle against wildfires
events.summary: French firefighters have won out over a massive blaze, with almost 200,000 evacuees returning home. But Europe's climate-fueled wildfire season is far from over.

events.title: Hungary to shut sole nuclear plant for first time on Sunday
events.summary: Record-low water levels on the Danube forced the Paks plant offline, leaving Hungary facing a potential power crunch. In neighboring Serbia, energy production at two hydroelectric plants has also been reduced.

events.title: How does eastern Europe commemorate the Roma Holocaust?
events.summary: In 2015, the EU designated August 2 as the European Roma Holocaust Memorial Day. In Germany, the day is marked with memorial services, educational activites and public addresses. And in eastern Europe?

events.title: Germany's long road to equality for same-sex couples
events.summary: In 2001, same-sex couples in Germany were able to register a civil partnership for the first time. The Civil Partnership Act was a crucial step toward "marriage for all," which was introduced in 2017.

events.title: Germany widens deportations to Afghanistan
events.summary: Earlier this week, Germany for the first time deported a man with no criminal record to Kabul. Faridoon Tofan, who is currently in deportation detention, fears the same fate.

events.title: More women die in heatwaves, but biology 'isn't main cause'
events.summary: In country after country, more women are dying from the heat than men. But researchers say biology isn't the main reason. Age, working conditions, and unequal access to rest may drive the gap.

events.title: War in Ukraine: Why Crimea has become a strategic target
events.summary: Ukraine has stepped up attacks on Russian logistics centers and energy facilities in Crimea. What are the consequences for local supplies, and how does Kyiv hope this strategy will affect the course of the war?

events.title: Germany weighs the future of minijobs
events.summary: Germany's popular minijob system allows millions of workers, including students, to avoid paying income tax or social security contributions. But a reform is on the cards that may soon end this advantage.

events.title: What's really causing Europe's wildfires
events.summary: From Greece to France, Europe is burning. But what's the real reason for the historic blazes ripping through the continent and why are they getting harder to stop?

events.title: From petitions to memes: How students made dissent visible
events.summary: From imperial China to present-day India, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols of their age to challenge authority.

events.title: Humanoid robots: Trump's latest China trade battle?
events.summary: The US has banned foreign-made humanoid robots, a market Chinese tech firms dominate. Although Washington cited national security risks, analysts think Donald Trump is buying time for US robot makers to catch up.

events.title: Eco wins: From death strip to nature haven and other green surprises
events.summary: A Cold War relic becomes a biodiversity haven, a Pokemon Go for trees and seagrass gets a second life. This week's eco wins come from some unexpected places.

events.title: FIFA plans: Infantino under pressure as senior advisor quits
events.summary: After regional football federations condemned FIFA plans for private investment, Carlos Cordeiro, senior advisor to FIFA President Gianni Infantino, tendered his resignation.

events.title: German court rules that AI music firm Suno violated copyrights
events.summary: Germany's state-mandated licensing agency, GEMA, says the verdict has "global significance," as Suno is also directed to pay yet-to-be-quantified damages.

events.title: Spain's PM visits Ceuta after thousands breached border
events.summary: Thousands of people continued pouring into Ceuta from Morocco during the night, after Spanish police lost control of the border. The head of the city government estimated that 60,000 people had entered.

events.title: Giving birth in Serbia: 'You leave your dignity at the door'

events.title: Yan Diomandé makes history with Real Madrid move
events.summary: Real Madrid have officially announced the signing of Yan Diomandé from RB Leipzig on a deal running until 2033. At just 19 years old, the Ivory Coast international also becomes the most expensive African player of all time.

events.title: Social media giant Meta ordered to pay $567 million in New Mexico child safety ruling
events.summary: A New Mexico judge on Thursday ordered Meta to pay more than $500 million, finding the social media company created a public nuisance and harmed children. The ruling follows a March jury verdict awarding the state $375 million after finding Meta liable for exposing children to online predators and other harms.

events.title: Middle East live: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey set to sign defence pact in Jeddah
events.summary: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey are set to sign a joint defence agreement on Friday in Jeddah, according to Saudi military and government sources. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif will meet in the Saudi port city as regional powers seek to strengthen security ties amid the Iran war. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.

events.title: US-backed Venezuela political transition talks begin without Nobel laureate Machado
events.summary: US-backed negotiations between Venezuela's interim government and a faction of the opposition began on Thursday after nearly a week of delays, the two sides said. events.title: Trump targets 'birth tourism' in new bid to curb birthright citizenship
events.summary: US President Donald Trump on Thursday signed an executive order targeting what he described as "birth tourism," seeking to curb birthright citizenship by restricting entry for pregnant visitors intending to give birth in the United States. Trump said the move followed the Supreme Court's rejection of his earlier effort to limit the constitutional right.

events.title: Bus explosion near Damascus kills at least two, injures 13
events.summary: At least two people were killed and 13 wounded when a bomb planted on a minibus exploded on Thursday in the Syrian town of Jaramana, near Damascus, state media reported, citing the health ministry. The blast tore off the vehicle's roof, wrecked its interior and scattered debris across the road.

events.title: 308 abductees freed from separate attacks in Northern Nigeria
events.summary: First, Nigerian security forces say that they've returned 308 abductees home after freeing them from their kidnappers in a northern forest. And, in Lagos, a Nigerian artist is turning ordinary clay into vibrant portraits, blending science, tradition and creativity in a technique he hopes will redefine the canvas.

events.title: Houthi rebels kill dozens of Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces
events.summary: At least 38 members of the Yemeni government forces were killed Thursday in drone and missile attacks carried out by Houthi rebels, according to medical sources. events.title: What to know about the total solar eclipse on August 12

events.title: FIFA closes ranks round Infantino amid mounting leadership crisis

events.title: Leftist Democrat urges unity after defeating establishment candidate in Michigan primary

Sudan’s ongoing war is threatening the integrity of its ancient Meroe pyramids, a UNESCO World Heritage Site known for its unique and angular architecture, as preservation efforts have completely halted.

“The site may face a disaster and collapses are possible,” warned archaeologist Mahmoud Suleiman.

Meroe, located some 200 kilometers (125 miles) north of the capital Khartoum, comprises over 200 pyramids built between 800 B.C. and 350 A.D. as royal tombs for the rulers of the Kingdom of Kush. 

“The sand has thickened heavily on the pyramids and even inside the temples, and the grass grows thick,” Mustafa Ahmed, one of the guards at Meroe, told The Associated Press as he made his way through sand dunes on site. “The pyramids have deteriorated greatly and stones have begun to fall.”

events.summary: The White House says a deal to get the Strait of Hormuz back open could be on its way as Treasury Secretary Bessent says he's had talks with Iranians to move to a "more normalized position in this conflict." NBC News' Keir Simmons reports.

events.title: Video shows drone chasing Ukrainian man around van before exploding
events.summary:
Video shows drone chasing Ukrainian man around van before exploding
Ukrainian authorities have released video said to show a Russian drone being used to deliberately chase and target a civilian. The 52-year-old farmer and market trader was wounded but survived the attack.

events.title: Trump administration revokes Brazilian ambassador’s visa in diplomatic dispute
events.summary: The Trump administration revoked the visa of Brazil’s U.S. ambassador Tuesday — the latest jab in a monthslong diplomatic spat between the two countries.

events.title: Trump claims Iran talks are underway as Tehran denies it

events.title: East Asia is baking in ‘cruelly hot’ summer
events.summary: A deadly heat wave is gripping large parts of East Asia, bringing the hottest temperature on record in South Korea and complicating earthquake recovery efforts in Japan.

events.title: Trump calls Iranian leadership ‘extremely duplicitous’ after Tehran denies new talks will start Monday
events.summary: Iran said it wasn’t holding talks with the U.S. but was in discussions with Oman over a temporary safe route through the Strait of Hormuz.
